motivation: Observable precise channels have many more peak-pair matches than precursor matches; current coarse contextual full unknown result has not preserved external proposal ranking benefit. Test information in peak-loss identity separately from original evidence strength gate and context head capacity.
hypothesis: Matched masking of all8 peak_loss identities may reduce spurious common peak-pair associations while retaining observed ion and precursor-loss identities.
training: Same original60K RNG42 representative spectra, fixed3epochs, AdamW .001 wd.01, correction792->64->2048, all original base tensors frozen; precise feature vector unchanged before mask; original maximum evidence strength gate retained.
comparison: All-channel precise contextual and all-identity-masked contextual; finalized complete cache-retry reports only.
limitations: Because the precise maximum gate is retained, masked peak channels can still supply evidence presence/strength. This tests their chemical identity information; it is not a claim to eliminate all peak-loss influence.
cohorts: Same2000 unknown and1340 known, no fresh holdout opened; current verified best and independently completed original control gates unchanged.
sequence: 241 precursor/ion identity residual training with matched peak-loss mask
